title: Safe Lock Face and Handle Condition (Close-up)
prompt:
1) Function (1 sentence)
Capture a forensic-quality close-up color photograph documenting the condition of a safe’s lock face and handle, with visible scale and unobtrusive annotations.

2) Scene / Composition (3–5 sentences; include subject percentage in frame)
Single still image of a fictitious metal safe door section filling the frame, centered on the circular lock face and adjacent handle. The lock face and handle together occupy ~75% of the frame, with a small portion of surrounding painted safe door visible for context. Place an L-shaped forensic scale with alternating black/white markings along the lower-left edge, lying flat on the same plane as the lock face. Add simple annotation arrows and short labels (e.g., “scratch,” “paint transfer,” “handle wear”) near observed marks without covering the lock face. Lighting is forensic flash with even illumination and minimal shadows.

3) Angle & Distance (strict numeric values)
Angle: 10° off perpendicular to the safe door plane (near-straight-on). Subject distance: 0.55 m.

4) Optics & Technique (lens mm, f/, 1/x s, ISO, WB K, focus, DOF)
Lens: 60 mm macro; aperture f/11; shutter 1/125 s; ISO 200; white balance 5600 K. Focus locked on the lock face engraving area; deep enough depth of field to keep lock face, handle, and scale markings sharp. Forensic flash used as primary light, diffuse and color-neutral.

5) Mandatory elements (labels/markers/timestamps already present in the case)
Include only: a forensic L-shaped scale (no agency name), and neutral annotation arrows with generic labels (“scratch,” “wear,” “smudge”). No timestamps, case numbers, camera IDs, or location labels.

6) Negatives (objective list of what MUST NOT appear)
No people, faces, reflections showing a person, fingerprints/palmprints in high detail, or identifiable biometrics. No real brand names, logos, model plates, serial numbers, or recognizable safe manufacturer markings. No readable caseId/evidenceId text, no dates/times, no police/official badges, no weapons, no gore/violence. No real license plates, no identifiable documents, no extraneous props (keys, phones, tools) unless already implied (not included).

7) Acceptance checklist (objective, verifiable bullets)
- Single color photo, forensic/neutral documentary look (non-artistic).
- Lock face and handle occupy ~75% of frame; surrounding safe door visible.
- Forensic flash look: even illumination, minimal harsh shadowing, accurate color.
- L-shaped black/white scale visible with clear markings, lying on same plane.
- Simple annotation arrows with generic labels present and not obscuring key details.
- No brands/logos/serials, no people/faces/reflections, no timestamps or IDs.
- Image is sharp on lock face, handle, and scale; minimal noise and distortion.
